messages.subject: StanCon 2017 notebooks
parts:
I missed that they were posted, so I just thought I'd let
everyone else know they're available through a GitHub
repo with a convenient top-level readme with summaries:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stancon_talks

They're organized by presenter with all the source code and
compiled notebooks linked, along with a link to the video
presentation at StanCon.

All of the talks are also on mc-stan.org in HTML form, with
index page here:

http://mc-stan.org/events/stancon

We're about to reorganize the case studies now that there
are dozens of them.

We're really trying to build up a set of case studies like
this because in our experience, if people can find one of
these related to what they want to do, it's a huge leg up
compared to having to work models out from first principles.

Instructions for submitting ones you might have are here:



- Bob
